memory_candidates.content: A PreToolUse hook that must be hermetically testable cannot call agent-system scripts that source deploy-root-guard.sh (which exits 1 when run from the source store) or that anchor PROJECT_ROOT to their own SCRIPT_DIR rather than the caller's cwd -- e.g. task-lock.sh. The testable pattern is to read the runtime record files directly and cwd-relatively (find specs -maxdepth 3 -name holder.json ..., specs/.sessions/*.json), inlining the portable liveness idiom (kill -0 on the recorded pid plus a heartbeat-age parse with a BSD date fallback) instead of reusing the script that owns it.

Before adding substantial prose to a file matched by an eager rule glob (.claude/rules/**/*.md with a broad paths: frontmatter, e.g. paths: ["specs/**/*", ".claude/**/*"]), check 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' against orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes BEFORE writing, not after. That baseline is a fixed, deliberately-reviewed ceiling (never silently re-derived), and a verbose new rule section can blow through the entire headroom in one edit. When it does, the established fix in this codebase is the eager-core/lazy-narrative split already used by rules/git-workflow.md and its companion context/standards/git-workflow-narrative.md: keep only the rule statement, a one-sentence distinguishing clause, a brief permitted-forms summary, and an enforcement/pointer paragraph in the eager file; move the incident record, the complete permitted-forms list, and practical guidance to the lazy companion.
